correctness.rationale: For all real a,b the smooth polynomial flow has f=1-x²-y² with df/dt=-2fxy(y-ax+z), preserving the open cylinder. Inside, |z dot|≤1+|b| gives complete two-sided solutions. For a≠0 the exact identity d(z+2x/a²)/dt=f[f+(x-y/a)²+(1+a^{-2}-b)y²] is strictly positive for b≤1+a^{-2}; for a=0, d(z+bx)/dt=f. Strict monotonicity excludes compact invariant subsets. If the monotone quantity is bounded, f² is integrable and f uniformly continuous, hence f→0; if unbounded, z→+∞. For a≠0 and b>1+a^{-2}, two explicit equilibria are strictly interior. All symbolic identities and endpoint substitutions passed the packaged actual-path checker; infinite-time conclusions are proved analytically.

value.rationale: The equilibrium cylinder is the defining object of an established numerical chaotic-flow family. Existence of isolated interior equilibria does not determine whether periodic, chaotic or other compact recurrent dynamics can occur without equilibria. The theorem gives a sharp all-real-parameter threshold that rules out every compact invariant subset below it, including the sign-indefinite vertical-speed regime 1<b≤1+a^{-2}; and determines the precise asymptotic alternatives for every interior trajectory in that region. This is substantive global dynamics and a natural complete qualitative classification, not an arbitrary numerical slice or restatement of the equilibrium census.
